slides.title: Welcome! What is Prompting?
content: If you're not a coder, this is your single most important skill for using AI.
Prompting is the art and science of giving specific instructions to AI.
narration: Welcome! If you're not a coder, this is your most important skill for using AI.
Think of an AI model like a super-smart and fast intern.
It can do amazing things, but needs very specific instructions.
Prompting is the art and science of giving those instructions.
This helps you get the high-quality results you want. Let's begin!
slides.image_prompt: Illustration of a busy cartoon person delegating tasks to a friendly AI robot assistant. The person looks relieved, and the AI robot looks ready to work.

slides.title: The Anatomy of a Good Prompt: The 3 C's
content: A weak prompt gets a weak answer. A great prompt gets a great answer.
The best prompts almost always include three key ingredients: Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
narration: A weak prompt gets a weak answer. A great prompt gets a great answer.
The best prompts almost always include three key ingredients.
These are Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
slides.image_prompt: A graphic showing three interlocking 'C' shapes, each distinctly labeled 'Clarity', 'Context', and 'Constraints'. They are vibrant and visually appealing.

slides.title: 1. Clarity: Be Specific!
content: The AI doesn't know what you're thinking.
Vague prompts lead to generic, unhelpful answers.
narration: Let's start with Clarity. Imagine you ask a chef to 'make food.'
What will they make? It's too vague, right? They will probably make something basic.
The AI is similar. It doesn't know what you're thinking.
Vague prompts lead to generic, unhelpful answers.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon chef scratching head, looking confused by a vague order like 'Make food!' in a speech bubble. Kitchen background.

slides.title: Clarity: Examples
content: Weak Prompt: 'Write about electric cars.'
Good Prompt (Clear): 'Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city.'
narration: For instance, a weak prompt is: 'Write about electric cars.'
A clear prompt details top three benefits of owning an electric car.
It specifies for someone living in a city. See how specific it is?
slides.image_prompt: Split screen. Left side: A large, blurry thought bubble with 'electric cars'. Right side: A sharp, focused spotlight on a detailed image of a city car with a clear label 'Top 3 benefits for city owner'.

slides.title: 2. Context: Give it Background!
content: Context tells the AI why you're asking and who the audience is.
It helps the AI adopt the right perspective.
narration: Next, let's talk about Context.
Imagine you are a tour guide explaining a historical monument.
If your audience is a group of historians, you would give detailed facts.
But if it's a group of children, you would simplify and make it fun.
Context tells the AI why you're asking and who the audience is.
It helps the AI adopt the right perspective.
slides.image_prompt: Side-by-side cartoon illustration: On left, a tour guide explaining a historical monument with detailed facts to a group of serious historians. On right, the same tour guide explaining the monument with simple, fun stories to a group of curious children.

slides.title: Context: Examples
content: Good Prompt: 'Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city.'
Better Prompt (with Context): 'Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city.'
narration: Here is our good prompt again. It asks for a blog post on electric car benefits.
Now, let's add context. We specify it's for a sustainable lifestyle blog.
This guides the AI to write from a specific viewpoint.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: A chat window showing a prompt being refined. The text 'for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living' is highlighted as if being added to an existing prompt.

slides.title: 3. Constraints: Set the Rules!
content: Constraints are boundaries that shape the output.
Tell the AI the length, format, and style you need.
narration: Finally, Constraints. Think of an artist creating a painting.
They might get a specific canvas size, or use only certain colors.
These are constraints. They shape the AI's output.
Tell the AI the length, format, and style you need.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon artist working on a canvas. Next to them is a blueprint showing specific canvas dimensions, a color palette, and a clock icon, representing creative limits.

slides.title: Constraints: Examples
content: Better Prompt: 'Write a short blog post for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city.'

Excellent Prompt (with Constraints): 'Write a short blog post, under 400 words, for a lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable living. Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for someone living in a city. Use a friendly and enthusiastic tone and end with a question to encourage comments.'
narration: Let's take our better prompt. It's for a sustainable lifestyle blog.
It explains electric car benefits for city residents.
Adding constraints makes it excellent. We ask for under 400 words.
Also, a friendly, enthusiastic tone, ending with a question.
slides.image_prompt: Three distinct pieces of paper, side-by-side, visually demonstrating how the output becomes more refined with each C added (Clarity, Context, Constraints). The last paper is notably more detailed and structured.

slides.title: Bonus Tip: Persona & Examples
content: Provide a Persona: Tell the AI who to be.
Giving Examples: Zero, One, and Few-Shot Prompting.
narration: Here's a bonus tip: Provide a Persona. Tell the AI who to be.
For example, act as an expert travel agent.
Create a 5-day itinerary for Rome. This is for a solo traveler loving history and food.
Now, let's look at Giving Examples: Zero, One, and Few-Shot Prompting.
This refers to whether you give the AI an example to follow.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon AI robot wearing different hats (e.g., chef hat, detective hat, travel agent hat) to represent adopting various personas, side-by-side.

slides.title: Zero, One, and Few-Shot Prompting
content: Zero-Shot: You give zero examples.
One-Shot: You give one example to show the AI the pattern you want.
Few-Shot: You give a few examples to teach the AI a more complex pattern.
narration: Zero-Shot means you give zero examples. Most prompts are like this.
You just ask for what you want.
One-Shot means you give one example to show the AI the pattern you want.
This is great for specific formatting.
Few-Shot means you give a few examples to teach the AI a more complex pattern.
slides.image_prompt: A sequence of three small frames. First frame: A blank box (zero examples). Second frame: A text box with one clear input-output example. Third frame: A text box with three input-output examples.

slides.title: Advanced Prompting: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
content: Asking the AI to 'Think Step-by-Step' dramatically reduces errors.
narration: You can refine your interactions with AI further using advanced techniques.
The first one is Chain-of-Thought, or CoT.
This means asking the AI to 'Think Step-by-Step.'
Imagine a detective solving a complex mystery. They don't just jump to a conclusion.
They list all the clues, connect them, then deduce the answer. This is how CoT works.
slides.image_prompt: Cartoon detective with a magnifying glass, looking at a board filled with interconnected clues and notes. A speech bubble above their head says: 'Think step-by-step!'

slides.title: CoT Example & Structuring Output
content: CoT Example: 'I have 5 boxes of apples. Each box has 12 apples. I eat 3 apples and give away one full box. How many apples are left? Think step-by-step.'
Structuring the Output: Tell the AI how to organize it to save time.
narration: For problems involving logic, math, or reasoning, this technique is very effective.
For example, consider the apple problem shown on screen. Use 'Think step-by-step.'
Now, let's look at Structuring the Output.
Don't just ask for information. Tell the AI how to organize it.
This saves you a lot of time.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen. Left: Animated sequence showing 5 boxes of apples, then some disappearing, then a question mark. A thought bubble shows a brain icon. Right: A cartoon librarian neatly organizing books into specific, labeled sections (e.g., 'Fiction', 'Non-Fiction', 'Biography').

slides.title: Structuring Output & Iterative Prompting
content: You can ask for formats like: A numbered list, HTML code, JSON, A simple comma-separated list.
Iterative Prompting: It's a Conversation! Refine prompts based on AI's output.
narration: You can ask for formats like a numbered list, HTML code, JSON.
Or, a simple comma-separated list.
For example, list pros and cons of remote work. Ask for a Markdown table.
Finally, Iterative Prompting. Think of a tailor making a dress.
They create a rough design, show it to the client, get feedback, then refine it.
Your first prompt is rarely your last. The real skill is in refining prompts.
Base your refinements on the AI's output. Treat it like a conversation.
slides.image_prompt: Split screen. Left: AI providing a neat markdown table as output. Right: Cartoon tailor adjusting a dress on a mannequin, with a smiling client giving feedback, showing a back-and-forth process.

slides.title: Iterative Prompting Example & Practical Lab
content: You: 'Write a slogan for my new coffee shop.'
AI: 'Brewing Happiness, One Cup at a Time.'
You: 'That's good, but can you make it shorter and more modern?'
AI: 'Urban Brews. Your Daily Grind.'
You: 'Perfect!'
Practical Lab: Your Turn!
narration: You can start with 'Write a slogan for my new coffee shop.'
If the AI says, 'Brewing Happiness, One Cup at a Time.'
You can then say, 'That's good, but can you make it shorter and more modern?'
And the AI might reply, 'Urban Brews. Your Daily Grind.' You: 'Perfect!'
Now it's time to practice.
slides.image_prompt: A clear chat bubble conversation between a person icon and an AI robot icon, showing the back-and-forth refinement of a coffee shop slogan. The final slogan is highlighted.

slides.title: Text Generation Challenge
content: Combine a Persona, the 3 C's, and a Structured Output.

Prompt: 'Act as a fitness coach. Create a simple 3-day workout plan for a beginner who wants to exercise at home with no equipment. The goal is a full-body workout. Present it in a table format with columns for 'Day', 'Exercise', and 'Duration'.'
narration: Open up any AI tool like Google Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude.
Try this challenge: combine a persona, the three Cs, and structured output.
Use this prompt: 'Act as a fitness coach.'
Create a simple 3-day workout plan for a beginner. They want to exercise at home.
Present it in a table format.
slides.image_prompt: A clean screenshot of an AI chat interface with the challenge prompt clearly typed into the message box, ready to be sent.

slides.title: Image Prompting Introduction
content: Image tools like Midjourney or DALL-E 3 use the same principles but focus on visual details.
Be descriptive! Think like an artist.
narration: Next, let's try image prompting. Image tools like Midjourney or DALL-E 3 use similar principles.
But they focus on visual details. Be descriptive! Think like an artist.

slides.title: Image Prompt Challenge
content: Image Prompt Challenge: 'A close-up, photorealistic image of a cat wearing a tiny detective hat and magnifying glass, sitting in a library. The lighting is warm and cinematic.'
Start Experimenting! The more you practice, the better you'll get.
narration: Try this image prompt in an image generation tool.
It asks for a photorealistic cat detective, with a hat and magnifying glass.
Place it in a library. The lighting should be warm and cinematic.
Start experimenting! The more you practice, the better you'll get.
You now have the fundamental skills to get amazing results from any AI tool.
